text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Back and leg pain: neurological examination of the legs at every visit; red flags reviewed (new weakness, saddle numbness, bladder or bowel change, fever, weight loss) with instructions to come the same day if any appear; the outside MRI reviewed and no repeat imaging unless the deficit progresses; naproxen with food for two weeks then as needed; heat and staying active; no opioids, no muscle relaxants, no bed rest
  • Sports medicine consultation for the disc herniation and chronic back pain, the thumb base, a brain health baseline after repetitive head impacts, and an exercise prescription for life after heavy training
  • Physical therapy twice a week for six weeks (directional preference exercise, motor control and core strengthening), then a home program; a graded return to running and swimming
  • Thumb base: X-ray of the hand; topical diclofenac gel; hand-protection advice
  • Thumb orthosis for gripping work and at night, hand therapy exercises, and a corticosteroid injection only if pain persists
  • Weight and cardiovascular risk after heavy training: home blood pressure monitoring with a validated upper-arm cuff, twice a day for a week, before any diagnosis; a meal plan matched to his lower energy needs; lipids and HbA1c at intake; repeat risk assessment yearly
  • Exercise prescription: 150 to 300 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity (walking, swimming and cycling, then running) and strength training twice a week, with no sparring or other head impacts
  • Brain health baseline after repetitive head impacts: symptom inventory (headache, memory, attention, mood, behavior, sleep, balance), MoCA, PHQ-9, GAD-7 and PROMIS sleep at intake; no brain imaging without an indication; repeat yearly; traumatic encephalopathy syndrome is a research diagnosis and is not made on history alone
  • Mood and anxiety: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and again at twelve weeks; support for the change of life after retirement
  • Stomach on NSAIDs: stop naproxen; omeprazole for four weeks; stool test for Helicobacter pylori; no further oral NSAIDs; topical diclofenac continued

resource.title: Rocky Marciano synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care for a retired professional boxer: a 32-year-old former heavyweight champion, four months retired, comes in a few weeks after a lumbar disc herniation with sciatica, on a background of years of back pain, with an aching thumb base from an old fracture. The episode covers the history and neurological examination of low back pain with radiculopathy and its red flags; when imaging and surgical referral are and are not needed; exercise therapy, motor control training and a short NSAID course without opioids under the 1947 American College of Physicians guideline; post-traumatic osteoarthritis of the thumb base with a splint, hand therapy and topical diclofenac under the 1949 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation guideline; NSAID safety, with dyspepsia that follows unmonitored daily naproxen and its test-and-treat management; a brain health baseline after repetitive head impacts (symptom inventory, MoCA, mood, anxiety and sleep, no imaging without an indication, and traumatic encephalopathy syndrome as a research diagnosis); the metabolic change after a sudden end to heavy training, with weight, blood pressure confirmed by home readings, lipids and an exercise prescription; and anxiety screening that is negative.
